_about: Provenance + currency baseline for every legal framework this audit enforces. The monthly legal-watch agent (see LEGAL_WATCH.md) re-verifies each entry, diffs against this file, and flags material changes. Edit `last_verified` and `status` only from a sourced research pass, never by guess.
jurisdiction_focus: California (almost all DigitalCLIQ dealer clients). Federal rules are secondary context.

frameworks.name: California CARS Act
frameworks.authority: SB 766; Cal. Civ. Code §1784.20 et seq. (Title 1.5B)
frameworks.watch: Subsection pin-cites verified against chaptered text (leginfo) 2026-06-28: cancellation §1784.43(a)(1), add-on disclosure §1784.41(b), total-payable §1784.41(c)(1), extended-term warning §1784.41(d), anti-waiver §1784.21, gov-affiliation §1784.40(j), preapproval §1784.40(e), valueless add-ons §1784.42(a)(5). Deep list indices (e.g. the EV-oil-change enumeration) are high-confidence but worth a final eyeball; section anchors are solid. DMV consumer summary reviewed 2026-09-10: it lists 'remedy if advertised price isn't honored' (now CA-CARS-023, §1784.40(i)) and states fleet exemption as 'five or more units', which conflicts with §1784.31(f)(2) 'more than one vehicle in a single transaction'. Statute applied; re-check the fleet threshold on the next verification pass. CA-CARS-013 pin-cite corrected to (j). 2026-09-14: CNCDA Compliance Guide v1.2 (2026-08-07) and Webinar FAQ (2026-08-31) folded into rules/ca_hard_rules.json (CA-CARS-025 to -040, pin-cite fixes on 004/007/008/009/020) and checks/registry.py. CNCDA says the Guide is updated continuously through October 2026: re-pull from CNCDA Comply before 2026-10-01 and diff against the vault digest (Resources/automotive-guidelines/cncda-cars-act-guidance.md). Fleet threshold: CNCDA Guide Part 1 states the statute's 'more than one vehicle in a single transaction' test, confirming the statute over the DMV summary. No delaying or amending legislation pending per CNCDA FAQ Q69.

frameworks.name: Federal FTC CARS Rule
frameworks.status: VACATED (NADA v. FTC, 5th Cir., 2025-01-27) and formally WITHDRAWN from CFR (Fed. Reg. 2026-02-12). Not enforceable.
frameworks.watch: Watch for any FTC re-proposal (would require a new ANPR).

frameworks.name: California vehicle advertising law
frameworks.watch: 13 CCR §260, could NOT confirm whether amended in 2024-2026; verify manually. Also review the annual batch of CA dealer laws effective each Jan 1. 2026-09-14 (CNCDA Guide): Plus Disclosure (11713.1(c)(2)) is required verbatim on every web page displaying a price; advertised price is a ceiling under 11713.1(e) so date every offer; specific vehicles need VIN or license, stock number alone is insufficient (11713.1(a)); 11709.3 showroom list now effectively covers all website inventory; 11713.27 (SB 478 hidden fees) safe harbor limited to 11713.1(b) fees; 11713.13(f)(1)(E) manufacturer indemnity for preselected vendors.

frameworks.name: CCPA/CPRA privacy
frameworks.authority: Cal. Civ. Code §1798.100 et seq.; CPPA regulations
frameworks.status: in force; NEW regulations effective 2026-01-01 (GPC opt-out must be CONFIRMED as processed; sensitive PI expanded incl. neural data & under-16). ADMT obligations begin 2027-01-01.
frameworks.watch: Consider a check that the site confirms GPC processing. ADMT (automated decision tech) rules start 2027-01-01, relevant if a dealer site runs automated credit pre-qualification.

frameworks.name: ADA + California Unruh Civil Rights Act (website accessibility)
frameworks.authority: ADA Title III; Cal. Civ. Code §51 (damages §52); WCAG 2.1 Level AA
frameworks.status: in force; WCAG 2.1 AA is the litigation baseline; $4,000 per violation (Civ. Code §52)
frameworks.watch: AB 1757 (would codify WCAG 2.1 AA as the statutory standard and extend liability to web vendors) is PENDING, not law. Escalate if enacted.

frameworks.name: TCPA lead-form consent
frameworks.status: FCC one-to-one consent rule VACATED (Insurance Marketing Coalition v. FCC, 11th Cir., 2025-01-24). For CA dealers, prior express WRITTEN consent remains the safe standard, do NOT loosen.
frameworks.watch: Bradford v. Sovereign Pest (5th Cir., 2026-02-25) relaxed written-consent for telemarketing, but binds only TX/LA/MS, NOT California. Keep requiring written consent for CA lead forms.

frameworks.name: FTC Section 5 dealer advertising posture (post-CARS Rule)
frameworks.authority: FTC Act §5 (15 U.S.C. §45); TILA/Reg Z 12 CFR 1026.24; CLA/Reg M 12 CFR 1013.7
frameworks.status: active enforcement; March 2026 warning letters to 97 dealer groups; FTC staff Automobile Industry Pricing Transparency FAQs ISSUED September 2026 (14 questions, staff views, not binding): all-in price with only consumer-paid government charges excluded, doc fee inside the price at the highest mandatory amount, most prominent amount on SRPs and VDPs, calls and texts are ads, lease upfront processing fees in due-at-signing, not-on-lot labeling, representative photo limits, shared dealer/vendor/OEM responsibility; FTC Bureau of Consumer Protection staff remarks 2026-09-30 (Dingman, NAMVBC; via ComplyAuto 2026-10-05): government-fee test turns on who is legally obligated, electronic filing and emission charges in the price by name, 'in transit' means already shipped, CTA buttons beside the price only if they do not imply a lower price, savings claims scoped honestly, AI-generated ads carry the same duty
frameworks.watch: 2026-10-08: staff remarks of 2026-09-30 folded into rules/ca_hard_rules.json (ftc_reference.staff_remarks_2026_09_30; FTC-SAVE-001, FTC-CTA-001, FTC-AVAIL-003, FTC-AI-001; FTC-PRICE-001/003, FTC-ADDON-001, FTC-AVAIL-001, FTC-RESP-001, FTC-ENF-001 descriptions extended) and checks/registry.py (FTC-SAVINGS-SCOPE, FTC-CTA-LOWER-PRICE, FTC-INTRANSIT-STATUS). mcpeeks-site-watch check_catalog.py C02 updated the same day (closes the item left open 2026-09-16). Still open: ComplyAuto state-by-state list of excludable titling/smog/emission charges (promised, not published as of 2026-10-08); ComplyAuto 2026-09-21 webinar recording not yet reviewed; CNCDA response reconciling the CARS Act total price with the FTC most-prominent all-in price; any FTC enforcement settlement announcements. Re-check ftc.gov business guidance and complyauto.com monthly.
